beats.text: A requirement is something the system must do, or a property it must have.
Business requirements state high-level goals. Stakeholder requirements say what end users expect. Solution requirements describe the product, and they come in two kinds.
Functional requirements describe behavior: what the system does. The student shall display his weekly schedule. The mailing service shall send a welcome email.
Nonfunctional requirements describe qualities and constraints: how well, and within which limits.
No more than two level-one faults per month. That's reliability.
Available ninety-eight percent of business hours. Availability.
Six seconds or less, for five thousand users an hour. Performance.
A password of at least eight characters, with one upper-case letter and one digit. Security.
Runs on both Windows and Linux. Portability.
Implemented in Java: a constraint. Talks to a bar code reader: an external interface. Locks the login page after three failed attempts: error handling.
So ask one question. Does it say what the system does? Functional. Does it say how well, or under which limits? Nonfunctional.
All of them go into the Software Requirements Specification.
